data.description:
Make the bridge runnable locally, on GitHub Actions, and on Jenkins — and make that verifiable
in-session rather than by a future adopter.

rebar core currently shells out to `gh` (`_commands/fsck_repair.py:284,291`) with no `-R` and no
`cwd=`, so `gh` resolves the repo from process CWD. Under Jenkins the reconciler-pause precondition
for a DESTRUCTIVE repair is silently a no-op. That single defect is catchable by a unit test with
`gh` removed from `PATH`.

Research established that rebar's code is already essentially CI-neutral (zero reads of `JENKINS_*`,
`GITLAB_CI`, `BUILD_NUMBER`, or `CI` in `src/`; `GITHUB_*` appears three times, two in docstrings).
**The portability surface is the workflow wrapper, not the code** — ~185 of its 415 lines are logic.

Testing strategy, sized honestly:

- **Do NOT stand up Jenkins.** Not infeasible, but the evidence it adds is small and the cost is the
  one this repo has already paid: the existing Jira DC harness fails because `atlas-run` downloads
  ~917 Maven artifacts (~900 MB) from a live vendor at every cold start with no runner volume cache.
  All 4 scheduled runs failed. Testcontainers would not have saved it.
- **JenkinsPipelineUnit buys nothing here.** It MOCKS rather than executes; its declarative support
  is a hand-written subset that drifts; its `credentials` directive is literally a `// TODO` — which
  is exactly this Jenkinsfile's payload; adoption is ~0.1% and almost entirely shared-library repos.
- The Jenkins project does not validate its own Jenkinsfiles (0/10 sampled), and only 3-5 repos on
  all of GitHub lint one in CI. **505 of 938 Jenkinsfiles in the jenkinsci org are a thin
  `buildPlugin(...)` call** into a tested shared library — the Humble Object pattern, at scale.
- The closest analogue, `aws/aws-sam-cli`, ships Jenkinsfile templates and tests them with a
  golden-file comparison in Python. No JVM, no Groovy linter, no Jenkins.

Residual config sizes after the move: GHA ~85 lines, GitLab ~50, Jenkins ~75 — of which **~25-30
lines of Jenkins credential handling are irreducible** (three credential shapes, each needing its
own `withCredentials`, and no `::add-mask::` equivalent). Total ~210 across three providers versus
~900-1100 if the current shape were ported verbatim.

`fetch-depth: 0` CANNOT move — it parameterises `actions/checkout`, which runs before any Python
exists. But the entrypoint can ASSERT it: `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` returning true
must fail with the f193 citation. That is the single highest-value item in the move, because it is
the one bug the Humble Object actually prevents from recurring per-provider — a GitLab author who
omits `GIT_DEPTH: 0` gets no comment at all today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] One runner-agnostic entrypoint; the three configs invoke it and carry no logic beyond credentials, timeout and exit-code mapping
- [ ] `rebar` core requires no `gh` binary for any documented operation; `_reconciler_pause` uses the portable gate
- [ ] A contract test runs the entrypoint under scrubbed environments for {local, github-actions, jenkins, gitlab, bare} and passes identically
- [ ] The same test fails if any vendor variable is read or any `gh` invocation is required
- [ ] A shallow clone is REJECTED with a named error citing f193, not silently proceeded through
- [ ] `Jenkinsfile` and `.gitlab-ci.yml` are real committed files; docs reference them rather than duplicating them
- [ ] The shipped GHA artifact is the workflow rebar actually runs (or a reusable workflow both consume), so it is exercised every 20 minutes
- [ ] All three configs assert one exit-code table, one secret-name set, one timeout — each cross-checked against code, never hardcoded
- [ ] The Jenkinsfile `sh` body is asserted single-quoted (a double-quoted GString interpolates the secret before the shell sees it, defeating masking)
- [ ] `.gitlab-ci.yml` validates against GitLab's official JSON schema offline, using dependencies rebar already has
- [ ] shellcheck runs over script bodies extracted from all three configs and FAILS on an unparseable config (GitLab's own extractor returns true there; ours must not)
- [ ] Uncovered risks are documented as KNOWN GAPS outside the AC. Cite Trivy's `contrib/Trivy.gitlab-ci.yml`, which still pins v0.19.2 (Sept 2021) on alpine:3.11, referenced by none of its 21 workflows — five years of undetected rot in a security vendor's shipped artifact.
data.title: Make the bridge portable across local, GitHub Actions and Jenkins
